title: A Journey by Train
description: Four recordings about a train journey: planning, a station desk, a message and a station announcement.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · Planning the journey
parts.intro: You will hear Nam and his aunt talking about a train journey.

script.speaker: Aunt Lisa
script.text: Nam, are you ready for your first long train journey on your own?

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Yes, I think so. I'm going to Hue to see my cousins. How long does it take?

script.speaker: Aunt Lisa
script.text: About six hours. The train leaves at ten past nine and arrives at ten past three.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: That's a long time. I'll take my book and some cards.

script.speaker: Aunt Lisa
script.text: Good. I'll pack sandwiches and a bottle of water. You can also buy hot food on the train, but it's expensive.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Where will I sit?

script.speaker: Aunt Lisa
script.text: In coach four, seat twelve, next to the window. A kind lady called Mrs Ho will sit near you. She'll look after you.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Great! I'll phone you when I arrive.

parts.title: Part 2 · At the station
parts.intro: You will hear a woman buying a ticket at the station.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Good morning. Where would you like to go?

script.speaker: Passenger
script.text: Two return tickets to Oxford, please. One adult and one child.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: When are you travelling?

script.speaker: Passenger
script.text: This Saturday, coming back on Sunday evening.

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: The adult ticket is twenty-four pounds and the child ticket is twelve pounds.

script.speaker: Passenger
script.text: That's thirty-six pounds altogether. Is there a cheaper ticket?

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Yes, with a family card, you save a third. Do you have one?

script.speaker: Passenger
script.text: I'm afraid not. I'll pay the full price. Which platform does the train leave from?

script.speaker: Clerk
script.text: Platform three, at eleven fifteen. You'd better hurry. It's ten past eleven now!

parts.title: Part 3 · A message about a delay
parts.intro: You will hear Nam's uncle leaving a message about a delayed train.

script.speaker: Uncle Tom
script.text: Hello, Nam. It's Uncle Tom. I'm at the station, and I have some bad news. Your train is late.

script.speaker: Uncle Tom
script.text: There was a problem with the signals, so the train will arrive at four o'clock instead of three. Don't worry, it's safe.

script.speaker: Uncle Tom
script.text: I'll wait for you on the platform. If I'm not there, I'll be in the station café, near the flower shop.

script.speaker: Uncle Tom
script.text: Please stay on the train until it stops completely, and keep your bag close to you.

script.speaker: Uncle Tom
script.text: When we get home, we'll have a big dinner. Your cousins are very excited to see you. See you soon!

parts.title: Part 4 · A station announcement
parts.intro: You will hear an announcement at a railway station.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Attention, please. This is an announcement for passengers at Central Station.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: The ten forty train to the coast is delayed by twenty minutes. It will now leave from platform six, not platform two.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Passengers for the capital should go to platform four. That train will leave on time at eleven o'clock.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Please keep your bags with you at all times. If you see a bag without an owner, tell a member of staff.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: The café on platform one is closed today for repairs, but you can buy drinks from the machine near the main entrance.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Finally, we remind you not to run on the platforms. Thank you, and have a pleasant journey.
